chapter_findings.finding: Opening hypotheticals/questions are distinguished from the attributed SEA drawing event. The two later-event teasers are rs0005/rs0006.

RNPA p46 supports the Jet Eze aluminum frame, canvas bag, shelves and accessible compartments. Kelly 1943 application/1946 grant precedes the later story. Plath patent background supplies the separate-cart security/loading sequence; the narration confines it to his problem statement.

RNPA pp46–47 by Bill Emmer supplies the South Satellite encounter, drawing, Moon/Dutch promise, following-week no-discussion and next-week refusal, then the summarized independent development. No calendar day, prototype chain, refusal psychology or production contract is added.

Patent pp10–11 and FIG8 support two recessed wheels, plate/axle/retaining tabs/openings, wheel wells, support feet, approximately 30-degree illustrative tilt and flange purpose. No modern swivel casters, auto-brake, tested load or universal curb performance is claimed.

Patent pp11–12/FIG5 supports the offset guide friction/wedging and downward release. PDF p12 scan visibly prints 22½ × 14½ × 8 inches. rs0074 calls it one embodiment; rs0075 a stowage purpose; rs0076 preserves flight-specific limits.

RNPA p47 supports adjustable strap, attached bag resting on floor when upright and Emmer’s qualified balance explanation. Patent FIG7 and p12 support removable J-hook, strap slot and snaps; pp11–12 support expandable pleated outer pocket and soft-sided bulging. Recalled bag and patent embodiment are not certified as an identical specimen.

Global Traveler September 2007 interview attributes coworker requests to CEO Kim Ballis. Travelpro corporate history attributes garage/warehouse growth to 1989 and retirement/full-time business to 1991. Patent dates remain filing 1989-08-08 and grant 1991-02-26. The ending gives a bounded design interpretation and CTAs.

exceptions_and_attribution: RNPA2016 p46–47 is Bill Emmer’s later first-person recollection, not p48 Sharkey’s byline. Its same-crew/SEA narrative is retained as attributed memory, not contemporaneous flight or factory records.

Travelpro history says 1987; Robert Plath’s signed Chinook2024 p17 entry says 1988. Neither is chosen as a resolved exact invention date. rs0107 retains late 1980s/early 1990s; filing/grant dates do not adjudicate invention day.

LAT_DASH1993 has no raw original in this cache: its preserved receipt reports tunnel403. It was not newly read or used to approve any row; legacy HOLD evidence is not promoted to a current primary read.

ABC_PLATH2012 paragraph23 describes a luggage trolley screwed onto a hard-sided bag. This cached report was checked for the exception only; the R1 narration does not place that prototype before or after the SEA drawing encounters.

Cached PRIOR1917 is US1241890 removable locking grip-handle, not a wheeled suitcase; PRIOR1919 is US1291539 coal-bag with rolling bottom elements, not a travel-case design. Neither is narrated as a wheeled-suitcase predecessor here.

Patent/referenced prior art, product introduction, publication and invention day are distinct. No global-first or all-department-stores rejection claim, wife prophecy, unproved inner thought or generalized male shame is narrated.

All 5 author-added anchors use already-preserved original raw files; all quoted excerpts/hashes and locations were rechecked. PDF raw/layout extraction modes differ in column order and token spacing; the Kelly application-date spacing exception is resolved by layout extraction. Half-inch dimensions require the scan, because PDF text extraction drops the fractions.
